title: Logical operators and short-circuiting
learningObjectives: Explain logical operators and short-circuiting and write clear, safe expressions.

understand.concept: Logical AND (&&), OR (||), and NOT (!) combine or invert conditions. && and || short-circuit: they may return one of their operands rather than a boolean, and the right operand is evaluated only when needed. Nullish coalescing is a separate operator for null or undefined values.
understand.whyItMatters: Short-circuiting is useful for conditional execution but can create confusing expressions when side effects are hidden inside conditions. Convert explicitly to Boolean when a boolean result is required.
understand.analogy: Logical operators are decision gates: AND needs both conditions, OR needs at least one, and NOT reverses a condition.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; operator evaluation and coercion follow JavaScript precedence and conversion rules.

explain.narrative: The results are false, true, and true. AND and OR can also return operand values rather than only true or false.

examples.explanation: The results are false, true, and true. AND and OR can also return operand values rather than only true or false.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console or page displays the expression results described.

practise.guidedTask: Create a permission condition using && and a fallback using ||. Then compare || with ?? for zero and empty string.
practise.independentTask: Write a small program that uses the operator or numeric rule in a practical example. Predict results, run the code, and explain any coercion.
hints: Preserve valid falsy values when using defaults.
Validate numeric inputs and check finite results.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Logical operators and short-circuiting</title></head><body>
<script>const hasAccount=true;const verified=false;console.log(hasAccount&&verified);console.log(hasAccount||verified);console.log(!verified);</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which operator returns the first truthy operand or the final operand?
questions.explanation: Logical OR returns the first truthy operand, or the last operand if none is truthy.

questions.prompt: What should you do before using a value in a numeric calculation?
options: Assume it is already a valid number
questions.explanation: Explicit conversion and validation prevent invalid or imprecise values from entering calculations.
